t: In addition to other provisions applicable to appropriations under this head, without regard to any provisions of law or Executive Order prescribing minimum flight requirements. Coast Guard regulations which establish proficiency standards and maximum and minimum flying hours for this purpose may provide for the payment of flight pay at the rates prescribed in section 301 of title 37, United States Code, to certain members of the Coast Guard otherwise entitled to receive flight pay during the current fiscal year who have been assigned to a course of instruction of 90 days or more.

fable.w: The section authorizes Coast Guard regulations to provide for flight pay, and under the definition (and the worked example on "may by regulation") a grant of regulatory authority counts as participation even when discretionary. The tempting opposite reading is that this is an internal military pay matter in an appropriations rider with no outside party named, which is a real concern and makes this a close call. On balance the explicit authorization to act by regulation controls.
fable.s: Coast Guard regulations which establish proficiency standards and maximum and minimum flying hours for this purpose may provide for the payment of flight pay

opus.w: The section lets the Coast Guard decide through its regulations whether to pay flight pay. Under the worked examples, giving an agency authority to act by regulation counts as participation, even when the authority is optional (Example 6). The tempting 'No' reading treats this as a purely internal pay matter with no outside party. That reading has some force, because military pay rules are often exempt from public comment, but the regulation-authority rule in the examples points to 'Yes'.
opus.s: Coast Guard regulations which establish proficiency standards and maximum and minimum flying hours for this purpose may provide for the payment of flight pay
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is "No." This is an appropriations rider about flight pay for Coast Guard members. It is internal to a military service, and no states, experts or members of the public are named. That reading doesn't fully hold up against the worked examples. Example 6 treats any statutory authority for an agency to act by regulation as participation, even when the authority is optional ("may"), because rulemaking counts. Here the Coast Guard's regulations "may provide for" flight pay, so this is an authority to act by regulation. One real doubt remains: military personnel and pay rules are usually exempt from public notice and comment. If the standard requires real outside involvement, the answer could be "No." I'm therefore only moderately confident.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the payment of flight pay to Coast Guard members based on existing or future Coast Guard regulations. It does not require or recommend any consultation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making this decision. The only actors mentioned are federal employees (Coast Guard members) and the regulatory body itself (Coast Guard), which is part of the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Coast Guard regulations which establish proficiency standards and maximum and minimum flying hours for this purpose may provide for the payment of flight pay at the rates prescribed in section 301 of title 37, United States Code, to certain members of the Coast Guard otherwise entitled to receive flight pay during the current fiscal year who have been assigned to a course of instruction of 90 days or more.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Coast Guard regulations" implies a rulemaking process that could involve public comment. However, the text itself does not mandate public participation in the creation of those regulations; it merely states what those regulations *may* provide for regarding pay. Furthermore, the actors involved (Coast Guard members, Secretary of Defense/Coast Guard Commandant implicitly) are all inside the federal government. There is no mention of consulting with the public, states, or outside experts.
